verdicts.note: Auditor since 2018, elected with 61.60% in 2018 and unopposed in 2022 (S11, S12); runs on her record and qualifications (S1, S5). The maximal proven-record case at high confidence holds.

The reform axis is money and power in politics (PAC money, term limits, dark-money bans, RCV, direct democracy). S5 (administering election law as written) and S6 (the vote-at-home column) are election-administration positions, not positions on campaign money or structural political reform. Defending vote-by-mail does not place her at 'work the system' (coalition-building within party/donor structures). Same reasoning as the Lewis auditor refutation of Townsend's reform score.

Direction holds but low understates the evidence. She says it in two of her own sources: 'while keeping costs low' (S1) and a 'careful, compliant and conservative approach to taxpayer resources' (S4), and cites on-time annual financial reports with no findings (S5). That is a clear, repeated audit-and-restraint statement, so medium fits. The 2024 mail-sorter request (S7) was mostly grant-funded and does not reverse the direction.

First run for the office; says he lacks a professional background in the auditor's duties and 'I don't have the experience Larsen has' (S2, S4). Highest office held is precinct committee officer (S1). Display note: his highlight 'Raised $38,740 to Larsen's $6,900 through early October [S7]' cites S7, but in Simpson's dossier S7 is only his own PDC record (ca-2026-3395474); Larsen's $6,900.54 comes from her dossier's S13 or the contest file's S7. Better to give only his own total, or drop the comparison from his card. Other auditor display text checks out: primary 58.19% to 40.24% (S4), two-term incumbent since 2018, 'catastrophe' quote (S2).

Hand counting, proactive voter-list cleaning and opposition to vote-by-mail (S2, S4) are an election-administration agenda. None of it concerns PAC money, term limits, dark money, RCV or direct democracy, which is what the reform axis measures. Same pattern as the Lewis auditor refutation (Townsend: voter-roll audits, voter ID, no late ballots). 'Restoring transparency, community involvement, and verifiable results' (S1) is about vote counting, not money in politics, and his remark about holding Olympia accountable (S2) is a reason for running, not a reform proposal.

'Responsible stewardship of your money' (S1) and the alleged 'poor financial stewardship' in the office (S2) are explicit restraint/oversight statements. -1 at medium is appropriately modest given no specific audit program.
